answer: A strong defense is requiring every agent identity to post a refundable bond locked behind a cipher signature tied to one hardware-backed key. Creating a single identity is cheap, but spinning up thousands means locking a bond for each one and risking slashing when any of them misbehaves. Like a meadow that can only feed as many grazers as its grass allows, the bond supply caps how many fake identities an attacker can sustain, and every new inlet of clones must pay the same entry price, so a Sybil flood stops being profitable.
